Daniel retained Mary as counsel. Mary filed a motion to dismiss on the ground that Daniel had been prejudiced by the 25-month delay in obtaining the indictment. Thereafter, Daniel, with Mary present, appeared in court for arraignment and stated that he wished to plead guilty. The presiding judge, Esther, asked Daniel whether he understood the nature of the charges, possible defenses, and maximum allowable sentences. Daniel replied that he did, and Judge Esther reviewed all of those matters with him. Judge Esther then asked Daniel whether he understood that he did not have to plead guilty. Daniel responded that he knew that. The judge accepted the plea and sentenced Daniel to 25 years. One evening at home, after reading Psalms with her husband Timothy, Lydia begged Timothy to kill her to end her suffering. As they remembered their life together and reaffirmed their love for each other, Timothy tried to persuade Lydia not to give up. Lydia insisted, however, and finally Timothy held a gun to her head and killed her. The most serious degree of criminal homicide of which Timothy can legally be convicted is A no degree of criminal homicide. B involuntary manslaughter. C voluntary manslaughter. YOUR PICK D murder. The stem gives mercy and request, not a legally recognized mitigation trigger. Mercy, consent, and love do not convert a deliberate killing into voluntary manslaughter. ▌ THE ELIMINATION — CUT · CLASH · CALL CUT A “No degree of criminal homicide” conflicts with the stem’s visible killing and fails under the mercy-killing Gold Key. body: THE TRUE-BUT-WRONG PICK 5:58 2 / 3 CRIMINAL LAW & PROCEDURE · GALILEE GRILL Question ID: 14678_galilee_grill Paul, a Christian law student, had just lost his job at a private bar-prep tutoring company and was despondent. He was contemplating suicide. With his revolver in his jacket pocket, Paul went to a private restaurant near campus where a Bible-study group often met after class and drank until he was very intoxicated. He overheard Timothy, seated at the next table, telling Lydia, the server, that small tutoring companies sometimes had to downsize to stay open. Paul turned to Timothy and said, “Be quiet.” Timothy responded, “I can say what I want,” while shaking his finger at Paul. Paul became enraged, snatched the revolver from his pocket, and shot Timothy, killing him. A state statute defines first-degree murder as “knowingly causing the death of another person after deliberation upon the matter.” Deliberation is defined as “cool reflection for any length of time, no matter how brief.” Second-degree murder is defined as “knowingly causing the death of another person.” Manslaughter is defined as at common law. What crime did Paul commit? A Manslaughter, because there was a reasonable explanation for Paul’s becoming enraged. B First-degree murder, because deliberation can take place in an instant. C First-degree murder, because Paul contemplated taking a human life before be

buttons.text: AManslaughter, because there was a reasonable explanation for Paul’s becoming enraged.
BFirst-degree murder, because deliberation can take place in an instant.
CFirst-degree murder, because Paul contemplated taking a human life before becoming intoxicated.
DSecond-degree murder, because Paul knowingly caused Timothy’s death without deliberation.

body: THE TRUE-BUT-WRONG PICK 5:57 3 / 3 CRIMINAL LAW & PROCEDURE · FELLOWSHIP CUP Title: The Fellowship Cup At a weekly Bible-study dinner in their home, Lydia decided to kill her husband, Stephen, because she was angry about his infidelity. She obtained cyanide, a deadly poison. During dessert, Lydia poured grape juice laced with the cyanide into a glass, handed it to Stephen, and raised it in a warm toast about forgiveness. Stephen was moved by the toast. He set the glass on an end table and embraced Lydia. During the embrace, Lydia changed her mind about killing Stephen. She slid the glass behind a framed Bible verse on the end table, planning for Ruth, their housekeeper, to clear it away the next morning. Stephen did not drink the grape juice. The next morning, Ruth found the glass while cleaning. Rather than throw the grape juice away, Ruth drank it. Shortly afterward, she died from cyanide poisoning. In a common law jurisdiction, of what crime(s), if any, could Lydia be found guilty? A Attempted murder of Stephen and murder or manslaughter of Ruth. B Only attempted murder of Stephen. C Only murder or manslaughter of Ruth. D No crime. NO FORENSICS UNTIL THE CLOCK STOPS LOCK IT — VERDICT →
